context.fact: 88% of Australians expect their super and investments to be managed responsibly and ethically (up from 83% in 2022); 75% would consider switching funds if holdings did not reflect their values; 78% are wary of greenwashing.
context.date: RIAA From Values to Riches, March 2024

context.fact: Market Forces found Australia's 30 largest super funds roughly doubled holdings in companies expanding fossil fuels from $19bn (2021) to $39bn (2024), concentrated in Woodside, Santos and Whitehaven Coal — the most-cited campaign statistic used to mobilise members.

Greenwashing is now a regulatory theme: ASIC penalties against Mercer Super ($11.3m, Aug 2024, 'Sustainable Plus' options held fossil fuel, alcohol and gambling stocks) and Active Super ($10.5m, Mar 2025, held gambling, coal, oil sands and Russian stocks it claimed to exclude; Active Super merged into Vision Super on 1 Mar 2025).

Superannuation is now paid on Commonwealth Paid Parental Leave from 1 July 2025 — a reform campaigned for by HESTA, Aware Super, AustralianSuper and Industry Super Australia as the single largest lever on the gender super gap. ASFA median balances: men $186k vs women $129k at age 55-59.

200 Australians were killed at work in 2023; 76% of fatalities occurred in six industries — agriculture, public administration & safety, transport, manufacturing, health care & social assistance, and construction — which map directly onto the member bases of Cbus, BUSSQ, Team Super, First Super, Prime Super, HESTA and Aware Super.

funds.heritage: Formed 2006 from ARF and STA (ACTU / Ai Group sponsored); absorbed Club Plus (2021) and LUCRF (2022). Australia's largest fund.
funds.member_base: Broadest base in the system — roughly one working Australian in eight — with heritage concentrations in manufacturing, retail, hospitality, community services and contract cleaning.
funds.demographics: Not disclosed publicly in aggregate; the fund reports on female member engagement (c.200,000 women made voluntary contributions in FY25) and frames the gender gap as a member priority.

themes.evidence: Publicly backed super on Paid Parental Leave (from 1 July 2025) and runs Equal Pay Day member campaigns quoting the ASFA gender balance gap.
Perennial Market Forces target because of its scale; the ABC/Market Forces analysis singled out its increased Woodside position. Net-zero 2050 commitment; PRI and Climate Action 100+ signatory.

funds.heritage: Created Feb 2022 by the Sunsuper–QSuper merger; since absorbed Australia Post, Woolworths/Endeavour, CBA Group, Qantas, Alcoa, AvSuper and Oracle corporate funds.
funds.member_base: Two very different halves: QSuper's Queensland public servants, teachers, police and health workers (defined-benefit heritage) and Sunsuper's broad private-sector base skewed to Queensland retail, hospitality and SMEs; plus large corporate plans.
funds.demographics: Not disclosed in aggregate. Inferred: older, higher-balance public-sector cohort alongside a younger private-sector cohort.

themes.evidence: Net-zero 2050 commitment; large renewable and infrastructure book. Less targeted by member campaigns than peers, in part because of its public-sector heritage and sheer breadth.

funds.heritage: First State Super (NSW public sector) merged with VicSuper and WA Super in 2020, VISSF in 2021 and TelstraSuper in April 2026.
funds.member_base: Nurses, teachers, police, paramedics, firefighters and other state public-sector and 'essential' workers; now also former Telstra employees.
funds.demographics: About 70% women (UNSW BusinessThink interview with Aware's Chief of Staff). Board 73% women.

themes.evidence: Frames the 30–40% gender retirement gap as its defining member issue; retired women described as the fastest-growing group among the homeless.
Build-to-rent 'essential worker housing' programme offering discounted rent to nurses, teachers and police — an investment thesis built explicitly around who the members are.
Net zero 2050 with a 45% portfolio emission-intensity cut by 2030 (2020 base); divested thermal coal in 2020; states support for a 'fair and equitable transition for workers'.

funds.heritage: Founded 1988 for hospitality workers; merged Intrust, Statewide and Maritime Super. 320,000 active employers.
funds.member_base: Hospitality, tourism, recreation and sport — cafés, restaurants, hotels, clubs, gyms, events — now open to all industries. 264,000 new accounts opened in FY25 alone, a sign of a young, high-churn, casualised base.
funds.demographics: Age and gender not disclosed in the annual report. Inferred: among the youngest and lowest-balance memberships in the system.

themes.evidence: Called out by Market Forces (2022) over Santos exposure; Hostplus replied the critique was 'simplistic', pointed to $1.4bn of climate investments and its SRI option that avoids fossil fuels. Net zero 2050; engages 680+ companies a year.

funds.heritage: Higher-education sector fund; absorbed Australian Catholic Super in Dec 2022. Largely internally managed.
funds.member_base: University academics, researchers and professional staff, plus Catholic-sector employees; highest average balances among industry funds.
funds.demographics: Not disclosed in aggregate. Inferred: older, highly educated, high-balance, politically engaged.

themes.evidence: The most organised member climate campaign in Australian super: Market Forces' 'UniSuper Divest' (launched Jan 2020, 12,000+ member signatories, NTEU-aligned academics). UniSuper responded with net zero 2050, exclusion of >10% thermal coal miners and interim targets, which campaigners called insufficient. Still named the largest holder of fossil-fuel-expansion companies in the 2024 Market Forces analysis (11.5% of Balanced).

funds.heritage: Retail Employees Superannuation Trust, 1988; sponsored by the SDA union and major retailers.
funds.member_base: Retail and fast-food workers — supermarkets, department stores, quick-service restaurants — many in their first job.
funds.demographics: Around half of members are under 30 (Rest, July 2024). Inferred: majority women, low average balances, high proportion of part-time and casual workers.

themes.evidence: McVeigh v Rest (2018–2020): a 23-year-old member sued over climate-risk disclosure; settled Nov 2020 with Rest committing to net zero by 2050 and TCFD-aligned reporting — the case that put member climate expectations on every trustee's agenda. Rest has since committed $1bn to Quinbrook green infrastructure.
A young, majority-female, part-time workforce makes the gender super gap and super on parental leave core advocacy ground (with Industry Super Australia).

funds.heritage: Founded 1984 by building unions; sponsored by CFMEU, AWU, CEPU, AMWU and Master Builders. Absorbed Media Super (2022) and EISS (2023). Chair: Wayne Swan.
funds.member_base: Building, construction and allied trades — carpenters, labourers, electricians, plumbers, engineers — plus media/creative (Media Super) and NSW energy workers (EISS). 136,000+ default employers.
funds.demographics: Not disclosed in aggregate. Inferred: heavily male, physically hazardous occupations, high reliance on default death/TPD insurance.

themes.evidence: Construction is among the six industries carrying 76% of Australian workplace deaths; insurance for hazardous work is a core member proposition. ASIC sued Cbus (Nov 2024) and the Federal Court imposed a $23.5m penalty (Nov 2025) for delays affecting 7,000+ death and TPD claims — the single biggest member-trust story in the sector.
Cbus Property (c.$4.8bn) exists to 'invest back into members' industry'; the fund cites 110,000+ direct jobs created on its developments.

After the CFMEU was placed in administration (Aug 2024) APRA forced an independent review of Cbus's board and spending; CFMEU-linked directors resigned. Union representation itself became the press story.

funds.heritage: Health Employees Superannuation Trust Australia, 1987; absorbed Mercy Super (2022). Passed $100bn FUM in Oct 2025.
funds.member_base: Nurses, midwives, aged-care and disability workers, early-childhood educators, allied health and community services.
funds.demographics: About 80% women (HESTA, Sept 2024); women members earn 16% less than male members on average. Board 69% women.

themes.evidence: The sector's most explicit gender-equity investor: founded 40:40 Vision (40% women in ASX300 executive teams by 2030), campaigned successfully for super on parental leave and the 12% Superannuation Guarantee, and lobbies on aged-care and early-childhood pay.

Health-worker groups (Healthy Futures, Friends of the Earth, EDO) campaign for HESTA to divest Santos and Woodside; HESTA divested thermal coal, voted against Woodside's climate plan (2024) and its remuneration report and a director (2025).
Health care and social assistance is one of the six industries carrying 76% of workplace fatalities; HESTA's advocacy links safe staffing and pay in aged care to member outcomes.

funds.heritage: KKR/CBA-owned platform; trustee Avanteos Investments. Members declined 5% in FY25.
funds.member_base: Adviser-directed and employer-plan members across all industries; lifecycle MySuper by birth-year cohort.
funds.demographics: Not disclosed. Inferred: older and higher-balance than industry-fund averages, adviser-intermediated.

themes.evidence: Net-zero 2050 commitment; member-values pressure arrives mainly via advisers rather than campaigns.

funds.heritage: Marsh McLennan-owned; absorbed BT Super (2023), Lutheran Super and Holden Employees Super. 200+ corporate plans (Ford, Ampol, Chevron, ASX, Coca-Cola…).
funds.member_base: Employees of large corporates enrolled through workplace plans; broad white- and blue-collar mix.
funds.demographics: Not disclosed.

themes.evidence: ASIC's first greenwashing penalty: $11.3m (Aug 2024) after 'Sustainable Plus' options held 15 fossil-fuel, 15 alcohol and 19 gambling companies they claimed to exclude — the reference case on whether funds honour member values claims.

funds.heritage: Insignia Financial (formerly IOOF/NAB wealth); trustee NULIS. Members declined 5% in FY25.
funds.member_base: Adviser-directed and legacy employer-plan members across all industries.
funds.demographics: Not disclosed. Inferred: older, adviser-intermediated.

themes.evidence: Named among the three largest holders of fossil-fuel-expansion companies (MySuper Growth) in the 2024 Market Forces analysis.

funds.heritage: AMP Limited; trustee N.M. Superannuation. Members fell 11% in FY25.
funds.member_base: Legacy adviser and employer-plan members; lifecycle MySuper by birth decade.
funds.demographics: Not disclosed. Inferred: older cohort, in run-off.

themes.evidence: Post-Royal Commission reputation remains the dominant press theme; limited member-values campaigning.

funds.heritage: Merged with Spirit Super (itself Tasplan + MTAA) in Nov 2024; MIESF also folded in.
funds.member_base: Professional, administrative and managerial employees (CareSuper heritage) plus motor trades, Tasmanian public and private sector (Spirit Super heritage).
funds.demographics: Not disclosed. Board 55% women.

themes.evidence: Net-zero 2050 commitment; low profile in campaigns.

funds.heritage: Accumulation plan for Commonwealth public servants since 2005; CSC also runs the closed PSS/CSS defined-benefit schemes and ADF Super.
funds.member_base: Australian Public Service employees and Australian Defence Force members.
funds.demographics: Not disclosed. Inferred: Canberra-centred, stable employment, above-average balances.

themes.evidence: CSC's PSS Default was named second-largest holder of fossil-fuel-expansion companies ($1.17bn) in the 2024 Market Forces analysis, an awkward headline for a government-owned trustee.

funds.heritage: LGIAsuper merged with Energy Super (2021), rebranded 2022, absorbed Suncorp Super (2023).
funds.member_base: Queensland local-government employees, electricity-industry workers, and former Suncorp retail members.
funds.demographics: Not disclosed.

themes.evidence: Energy-sector heritage makes the coal-to-renewables transition a live member issue in Queensland; no major campaign recorded.

funds.heritage: Victorian energy/utilities heritage (SECV); merged Catholic Super and BOC Super in 2021. Trustee Togethr.
funds.member_base: Energy and utilities workers, Catholic education and health staff, industrial gases (BOC) employees.
funds.demographics: Not disclosed. Board 33% women.

themes.evidence: Legacy energy workforce; transition and job security sit alongside climate as member concerns.

funds.heritage: Victorian local-government fund (Local Authorities Super Fund); merged with NSW's Active Super on 1 March 2025 (post-merger membership larger than shown).
funds.member_base: Local council and water-authority employees in Victoria and NSW.
funds.demographics: Not disclosed.

themes.evidence: Inherited Active Super's $10.5m ASIC greenwashing penalty (Mar 2025) for claiming to exclude gambling, coal, oil sands and Russian stocks it held — a caution on values marketing.

funds.heritage: Mine Super (coal-mining heritage, 55,000 members) merged with TWUSUPER (transport, 99,000 members) in March 2025.
funds.member_base: Coal and hard-rock miners, truck drivers, bus and logistics workers, energy workers.
funds.demographics: Not disclosed. Inferred: overwhelmingly male, regional, hazardous occupations.

themes.evidence: Transport is one of the six industries carrying 76% of workplace deaths (vehicle incidents alone are 42% of all fatalities); TWU 'Safe Rates' and mine-safety campaigns define the sponsoring unions.
A coal-mining member base makes 'just transition' rather than divestment the salient framing.

funds.heritage: Telstra's corporate fund (c.$26bn) transferred into Aware Super in April 2026; retained here for the December 2025 snapshot only.
funds.member_base: Current and former Telstra employees and their families.
funds.demographics: Not disclosed.

funds.heritage: Non-Government Schools super; Catholic and independent school heritage plus community organisations.
funds.member_base: Teachers and support staff in independent and Catholic schools, early learning and community organisations.
funds.demographics: Not disclosed. Inferred: majority women (education workforce).

themes.evidence: Set a carbon-neutral portfolio target for 2030 (announced 2021), calling 2050 'misaligned' with the science; has excluded >30% thermal-coal companies since 2016.

funds.heritage: Rural and regional heritage; merged Combined Super (education) and Health Industry Plan.
funds.member_base: Farm and agribusiness workers, rural health, and education staff.
funds.demographics: Not disclosed. Board 50% women.

themes.evidence: Agriculture has Australia's highest workplace fatality rate (9.2 per 100,000 workers).

funds.heritage: Queensland building and construction industry fund since 1985.
funds.member_base: Queensland construction trades and labourers.
funds.demographics: Not disclosed. Inferred: heavily male, hazardous occupations.

themes.evidence: Same member risk profile as Cbus: construction fatalities and falls from height (up 71% in 2023) make default insurance the core proposition.

funds.heritage: Founded 1989 for the legal profession.
funds.member_base: Solicitors, barristers, paralegals and law-firm staff.
funds.demographics: Not disclosed. Inferred: high income, high balance; board 30% women.

themes.evidence: Professional membership; press coverage is about performance and mergers rather than values campaigns.

funds.heritage: Pharmacy Guild-owned; includes the Child Care Super brand.
funds.member_base: Pharmacy assistants and pharmacists, early-childhood educators, veterinary and allied health staff.
funds.demographics: Not disclosed. Inferred: strongly female, part-time, low balances.

themes.evidence: Markets itself around women in low-paid care and retail-health roles; the gender super gap is its stated raison d'être.

funds.heritage: Formed 2008; timber, pulp and paper, furniture and joinery industries (CFMEU Manufacturing heritage). Members grew 33% in FY25.
funds.member_base: Sawmill, forestry, pulp and paper, furniture and joinery workers, largely regional.
funds.demographics: Not disclosed. Board 50% women.

themes.evidence: Forestry and manufacturing both sit among the highest-fatality industries; First Super is known for vocal shareholder activism on worker treatment and executive pay.

funds.heritage: Founded 1986 on a published Ethical Charter; absorbed Christian Super (Nov 2022). ASX-listed parent.
funds.member_base: Self-selecting values-driven savers who chose the fund for its screens (no fossil fuels, weapons, tobacco, gambling; positive screens for health, education, renewables).
funds.demographics: Not disclosed. Inferred: younger and more female than the industry average; urban professionals.

themes.evidence: Values ARE the product: the Ethical Charter governs every holding; regularly cited as the benchmark ethical fund by campaigners.

funds.heritage: Founded 2014 by climate campaigner Simon Sheikh as Australia's first fossil-fuel-free fund; runs Verve Super (women-focused); owns smartMonday. Members grew 16% in FY25.
funds.member_base: Climate-motivated, mostly young Australians who joined through activism rather than employers.
funds.demographics: Not disclosed. Inferred: youngest member base in the universe.

themes.evidence: Launched at a climate rally; ran the 2019 'Not Business as Usual' climate-strike campaign with 3,000 businesses; positions itself on the RIAA statistic that 88% want responsible super.

funds.heritage: Formerly Aon Master Trust; acquired by Future Group in 2022.
funds.member_base: Employees enrolled through corporate plans; lifecycle default.
funds.demographics: Not disclosed.

themes.evidence: Owned by an ethical-fund group but sold as a mainstream corporate default; values positioning is muted.

funds.heritage: Launched Nov 2022; low-cost index proposition. Members grew 78% in FY25.
funds.member_base: Self-directed, cost-conscious savers, often younger and digitally engaged.
funds.demographics: Not disclosed.

themes.evidence: Parent Vanguard Investments Australia paid a $12.9m ASIC greenwashing penalty (2024) over an ethically-labelled bond fund (not the super fund); Vanguard globally exited the Net Zero Asset Managers initiative in 2022.

funds.heritage: Real Estate Institute heritage fund since 1975.
funds.member_base: Real-estate agents, property managers and agency staff.
funds.demographics: Not disclosed. Inferred: commission-based incomes, high churn.

themes.evidence: Small specialist fund; press coverage concerns scale and merger prospects rather than values.
